newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Wool markets seen recovering - NSW Farmers.
newsitem.headline: Wool markets seen recovering - NSW Farmers.

text.p: The world textile recession was easing in the United States, Britain and China, David Wolfenden, chairman of the wool committee of the New South Wales Farmers' Association, told its annual conference on Wednesday.
However, other major apparel markets including Germany, France and Japan remained subdued, he said.
John Ring, managing director of Wesfarmers Dalgety Ltd maintained the optimistic view in his address at the conference.
"Although volatility is a fact of life, the outlook for the wool market over the next few months is a lot more positive than the same time last year," he said.
The fundamental factors of improved demand from overseas mills, combined with a favourable exchange rate and continuing low levels of supply are all positive, Ring said.
Wolfenden said wool would remain a competitive textile fibre into the next century, but would not automatically have a market.
"Wool must earn its place in the sun, not demand it," he added.
Wool did not have a narrowly defined market, but must encourage a diverse range of competitive marketing pathways, he said.
"Without a sustained price recovery, wool production would continue to decline," Wolfenden said, referring to the 37 percent increase in the wool price over the 12 months to June.
